description: Pins the protocol::encode_prefs_blob_raw + protocol::decode_prefs_blob byte mapping for cross-implementation conformance. vault.prefs is the v0.1 vault-level singleton encrypted-preferences blob (MYP1 magic) carrying user-controllable preferences. The v0.1 inner schema (MYND-160 + MYND-183 + MYND-110) carries: screen_capture_protection (bool), deliberate_folders (sorted-set string array), auto_lock_seconds (optional integer), editor_layout (optional nested object), the unified manual-sidebar sequences favorites + item_order (item_order is HETEROGENEOUS — note UUIDs + canonical trailing-slash folder paths interleaved, replacing the pre-MYND-183 note_order/folder_order pair), theme (optional 'light'/'dark'/'amoled' string; absence ≡ system / follow-the-OS), and the decoration maps folder_icons (MYND-185 — nested string→string object: canonical folder path → icon name) + item_colors (MYND-184 — nested string→string object: a heterogeneous note-UUID-or-folder-path key → color-slot name). The device_names map (MYND-459 / SYNC-41 — a device_id-hex -> friendly-name string->string object, the folder_icons/item_colors precedent class) is an additive field omitted-when-empty. Canonical key order (partial, additive fields land at their lexicographic slot): auto_lock_seconds < deliberate_folders < device_names < editor_layout < favorites < folder_icons < item_colors < item_order < screen_capture_protection < theme; within each decoration/name object the members are emitted in lexicographic KEY order. Optional fields are omitted-when-default, so a screen_capture-only vault stays byte-identical to a pre-MYND-183 blob. The outer envelope is 34-byte fixed-offset (magic + protocol_version + reserved + 24-byte prefs_nonce + 4-byte big-endian ciphertext_len) followed by AEAD-wrapped canonical-JSON plaintext + 32-byte CTX commitment tag (Chan & Rogaway 2022). prefs_key derives from root_key via the canonical DeriveSubkey helper with HKDF context 'myne.v0.1 prefs-key' (no items_key coupling, see grill Q1). AAD binds account_number_hash + the role string 'prefs-blob' (39 bytes total). Read failure surface is non-distinguishing per spec §6.4 + §9.5.5: wrong key, wrong AAD, tampered ciphertext, tampered CTX tag all collapse to a single AeadFailure. Cases generated by `cargo test -p protocol --lib emit_prefs_vectors_for_paste -- --ignored` (in protocol/src/prefs.rs).

cases.description: Canonical encode case with screen_capture_protection=true (PrefsView::default(), the safer-state semantic per spec §9.5.5). Inputs use distinct byte patterns (root_key=0x42×32, account_hash=0x33×16, nonce=0x77×24) so any swap or off-by-one drift surfaces as a clear hex mismatch. Expected blob is exactly 100 bytes (34-header + 34-plaintext + 32-CTX-tag).

User-toggled-off case: screen_capture_protection=false. Same root_key + account_hash as encrypt-default but distinct prefs_nonce (0x88×24) so the encoded blob diverges in ciphertext bytes from the default case. Plaintext is 35 bytes UTF-8 ('false' is one byte longer than 'true'); expected blob is 101 bytes (34-header + 35-plaintext + 32-CTX-tag).

Round-trip with encrypt-default: the blob bytes from case 1 decode back to PrefsView{ screen_capture_protection: true } under the same root_key + account_number_hash. Verifies the full encode→decode pipeline byte-for-byte.

Cross-vault attack scenario: a vault.prefs encoded under vault A's (root_key=0x42×32, account_hash=0x33×16) bytes are placed in vault B's directory and the decoder is invoked with vault B's (root_key=0xAB×32, account_hash=0xCD×16). The decoder MUST report a non-distinguishing AEAD failure — both the prefs_key mismatch (different root_key) and the AAD mismatch (different account_number_hash) contribute, but the surface is a single CannotDecrypt outcome per spec §6.4 + §9.5.5. Implementations MUST NOT distinguish which mismatch fired.

Tamper-detection scenario: a single byte of ciphertext at offset 40 of the encrypt-default blob has been flipped via XOR 0xFF (changed from 0x91 to 0x6e). The decoder is invoked with the ORIGINAL root_key + account_number_hash. The CTX commitment construction (SHA-256 over key||nonce||AAD-len||AAD||Poly1305-tag) MUST detect the modification — the recomputed Poly1305 tag changes, the recomputed CTX commitment changes, the constant-time comparison fails. Output is a non-distinguishing AEAD failure indistinguishable (at the caller-visible surface) from cross-vault.

Fully-populated v0.1 schema (MYND-183 + MYND-308/299/348): every field set, exercising the unified heterogeneous item_order (note UUIDs + canonical folder paths interleaved) + favorites alongside deliberate_folders, auto_lock_seconds, editor_layout, the canonically-first active_workspace (MYND-308), and the editor batch fields editor_default_view_mode (MYND-299) + editor_focus_dim_inactive + editor_focus_typewriter (MYND-348). Same root_key + account_hash as encrypt-default; distinct prefs_nonce (0x99×24). Pins the canonical key order (active_workspace < auto_lock_seconds < deliberate_folders < editor_default_view_mode < editor_focus_dim_inactive < editor_focus_typewriter < editor_layout < favorites < item_order < screen_capture_protection) and the sequence-vs-set encoding discipline (item_order/favorites preserve order verbatim; deliberate_folders is sorted+deduped). The plaintext mirrors the spec §9.5.2 worked example.

Round-trip with encrypt-populated: the fully-populated blob decodes back to the same PrefsView under the same root_key + account_number_hash. Verifies the decode side reconstructs the heterogeneous item_order + favorites + the canonically-first active_workspace (MYND-308) + the editor batch fields (MYND-299/348) + all other fields in order (sequence arrays preserved verbatim; the omitted-when-default discipline is exercised by the other cases).

MYND-110 theme field: screen_capture_protection=true plus an explicit theme=dark. Pins the canonical key position of 'theme' (lexicographically LAST — t > s, so it follows screen_capture_protection) and its lowercase JSON-string encoding ('light'/'dark'). theme is Option<ThemeChoice> where absence is the canonical encoding of system (follow the OS), so this Some(Dark) case is the only shape that emits the key; a None/system vault stays byte-identical to encrypt-default (omit-when-None). Same root_key + account_hash as encrypt-default; distinct prefs_nonce (0xAA×24). Plaintext is 49 bytes UTF-8.

Round-trip with encrypt-themed-dark: the blob decodes back to PrefsView{ screen_capture_protection: true, theme: dark } under the same root_key + account_number_hash. Verifies the decoder parses the theme string after screen_capture_protection and maps 'dark' to ThemeChoice::Dark.

Encode case with the three MYND-191 daily-notes fields set (daily_date_format=YYYY-MM-DD, daily_folder=Daily/, daily_template=<uuid>) + screen_capture_protection=true. Pins the canonical key order daily_date_format < daily_folder < daily_template < screen_capture_protection and the omitted-when-default discipline (a vault without these fields encodes to the shorter encrypt-default blob). Inputs: root_key=0x42x32, account_hash=0x33x16, nonce=0xBBx24.
Round-trip with encrypt-daily: the blob decodes back to a PrefsView carrying the three daily-notes fields + screen_capture_protection=true under the same root_key + account_number_hash.

Encode case with the MYND-184 item_colors + MYND-185 folder_icons decoration maps set (+ screen_capture_protection=true). Pins the canonical key order folder_icons < item_colors < screen_capture_protection and the nested string→string object encoding: object members are emitted in lexicographic KEY order (folder_icons keys Archive/2025/ < Projects/Myne/; item_colors keys are heterogeneous note-UUID-or-folder-path, 0190a000-… < Projects/Myne/). Both maps are omitted-when-empty, so a vault without decorations encodes to the shorter encrypt-default blob. Inputs: root_key=0x42x32, account_hash=0x33x16, nonce=0xCCx24.

Round-trip with encrypt-decorations: the blob decodes back to a PrefsView carrying the folder_icons + item_colors maps + screen_capture_protection=true under the same root_key + account_number_hash. Verifies the decoder parses both nested string→string objects in canonical position (between favorites and item_order).

MYND-205 vault label. PrefsView carries item_order (two heterogeneous entries) + label; the label is supplied in NFD in the generator source ('Cafe' + U+0301 combining acute) and MUST encode as NFC ('Café', bytes 43 61 66 c3 a9) in the canonical plaintext. Pins the NFC normalization on encode AND the canonical key order item_order (i) < label (l) < screen_capture_protection (s). Generated by `cargo test -p protocol --lib emit_label_and_tolerance_prefs_vectors -- --ignored` (in protocol/src/prefs.rs).

Round-trip with encrypt-labeled: the blob decodes back to a PrefsView carrying item_order + the NFC label 'Café' + screen_capture_protection=true under the same root_key + account_number_hash. Verifies decoders surface the MYND-205 label field from its canonical position between item_order and screen_capture_protection.

Forward-compat (spec §9.5.2): the sealed inner plaintext carries a genuinely unknown additive field zz_future_pref (in sorted position after theme); decoders must ignore it and recover the known fields rather than rejecting. expected_plaintext_canonical_utf8_hex is the canonical re-encode of the decoded view WITHOUT the unknown field — NOT the sealed bytes, which live verbatim in informational_sealed_plaintext_utf8_hex. Generated by `cargo test -p protocol --lib emit_label_and_tolerance_prefs_vectors -- --ignored` (in protocol/src/prefs.rs).

MYND-58 last_backup_at field (vault-backup-restore epic): label + last_backup_at both set so the canonical bytes pin the relative order of the two 'l' keys (label [lab] < last_backup_at [las] < screen_capture_protection) and the bare-decimal u64 epoch-seconds encoding (1765432100, no trailing .0). Same vault-A inputs as the sibling cases (root_key=0x42x32, account_hash=0x33x16); prefs_nonce=0xF1x24, the next free entry in the family's nonce registry.

Round-trip with encrypt-last-backup-at: the blob decodes back to a PrefsView carrying label='Work' + last_backup_at=1765432100 + screen_capture_protection=true under the same root_key + account_number_hash. Verifies decoders surface the MYND-58 epoch field from its canonical position between label and screen_capture_protection, and that a u64-width epoch parses as a bare decimal integer (floats are FORBIDDEN per spec §9.5.2).
Only the 4-byte MYP1 magic — no room for the 34-byte header (magic + version + reserved + 24-byte nonce + 4-byte ciphertext_len). Rejected before any field read.
cases.informational_tamper_description: blob is the 4 magic bytes only (4 < 34)

cases.description: First byte of the MYP1 magic corrupted to 'X'. Rejected at offset 0 before any decryption — a foreign file, different artifact type, or forward-incompatible MYP5 blob all fail here.
protocol_version byte (offset 4) set to 0x02 instead of 0x01. A v0.1 decoder rejects an unknown protocol version before decrypting.

reserved byte (offset 5) set to 0x01 instead of 0x00. Spec §9.5.1 makes non-zero an unconditional parse rejection — reserved bytes are flag carriers for future v0.1.x revisions and a v0.1.0 client cannot honor unknown flags.

ciphertext_len field (offset 30..34) set to 0xFFFFFFFF, far above MAX_PREFS_PLAINTEXT_LEN + 32 (64 KiB + 32). The overflow guard rejects before any slice indexing — a port MUST bound-check ciphertext_len before allocating or indexing (DoS-allocation defense, §9.5.4).
Valid header advertising ciphertext_len = N, but the blob is one byte shorter than header + N. Rejected before the AEAD stage.
cases.informational_tamper_description: final byte dropped (blob shorter than header + advertised ciphertext_len)

cases.description: A structurally valid envelope sealed under the REAL prefs_key + AAD whose inner plaintext is 'this is not canonical json'. AEAD verification succeeds — the reject fires at the canonical-JSON parse stage. Distinguishable from CannotDecrypt because the tag check already proved the bytes came from a prefs_key holder (corruption past that point is structural, not adversarial). A port that returns its AEAD-failure error here has merged two distinct failure surfaces.

Encrypt a vault.prefs carrying one saved view (MYND-273, Saved Views) — a cards view over Books/ with a typed rating>4 filter AST, sort, columns, group_by, card_size, image, image_aspect_ratio (a STRING, since canonical JSON forbids floats) — plus a view_order. Pins canonical key positions saved_views (before screen_capture_protection) and view_order (last), the saved-view sub-object lexicographic key order, and the filter-AST encoding.
Round-trip with encrypt-saved-views: decoders must recover the saved view (filter AST, sort, columns, typed fields) and the view_order from the blob bytes of the encrypt case.

Canonical encode with theme=Amoled — the third explicit theme choice (a pure-black variant of Dark). Pins the lowercase variant string 'amoled' the serializer emits and the canonical key order (theme last). Same fixed vault-A inputs as the family; nonce 0xA0.

Round-trip with encrypt-themed-amoled: the blob decodes back to PrefsView{ screen_capture_protection: true, theme: Amoled }. Decoders must recognize the 'amoled' theme value (not fall through to None ≡ system).

editor-line-numbers (MYND-314) editor_line_numbers field: screen_capture_protection=true plus an explicit editor_line_numbers=true. Pins the canonical key slot of 'editor_line_numbers' (after editor_layout, before screen_capture_protection — editor_la < editor_line_n < s) and its bare-bool JSON encoding. editor_line_numbers is Option<bool> where absence is the canonical encoding of the prose-first default-OFF, so this Some(true) case is the only shape that emits the key; an unset vault stays byte-identical to encrypt-default (omit-when-None). Same fixed vault-A inputs as the family; nonce 0xF4.

Round-trip with encrypt-editor-line-numbers: the blob decodes back to PrefsView{ screen_capture_protection: true, editor_line_numbers: true } under the same root_key + account_number_hash. Verifies the decoder parses the editor_line_numbers bool at its canonical slot (between editor_layout and screen_capture_protection).

archive-disable archive_disabled field: screen_capture_protection=true plus an explicit archive_disabled=true. Pins the canonical key slot of 'archive_disabled' (after active_workspace, before auto_lock_seconds — ac < ar < au) and its bare-bool JSON encoding. archive_disabled is Option<bool> where absence is the canonical encoding of the default-OFF (archiving enabled), so this Some(true) case is the only shape that emits the key; an unset vault stays byte-identical to encrypt-default (omit-when-None). Same fixed vault-A inputs as the family; nonce 0xA7.

Round-trip with encrypt-archive-disabled: the blob decodes back to PrefsView{ archive_disabled: true, screen_capture_protection: true } under the same root_key + account_number_hash. Verifies the decoder parses the archive_disabled bool at its canonical slot (between active_workspace and auto_lock_seconds).

MYND-304 keymap overrides. PrefsView carries item_order + keymap (a string->array object: command id -> chord set) + label, pinning the canonical key order item_order (i) < keymap (k) < label (l) < screen_capture_protection (s), the inner lexicographic key order (app.command-palette < vault.lock), the set-canonical chord array (sorted Mod-k < Mod-p), and the explicit-unbind state (vault.lock -> [], preserved verbatim and distinct from an absent command). Same vault-A inputs as the sibling cases; prefs_nonce=0xF4x24. Generated by emit_keymap_prefs_vectors in protocol/src/prefs.rs.

Round-trip with encrypt-keymap: the blob decodes back to a PrefsView carrying item_order + the keymap override map + label under the same root_key + account_number_hash. Verifies decoders surface the MYND-304 keymap from its canonical position between item_order and label, parse the inner string->array object, and preserve the []-unbind entry verbatim.

A structurally valid envelope sealed under the REAL prefs_key + AAD whose inner plaintext gives a keymap value as a bare string (a.cmd -> "Mod-a") instead of an array. AEAD verification succeeds; the reject fires at the canonical-JSON parse stage (the chord set MUST be an array). Distinguishable plaintext_parse_failed, not a CannotDecrypt. Sealed manually (the typed encoder can only emit canonical v0.1 plaintexts); prefs_nonce=0xF5x24.
cases.informational_tamper_description: validly-sealed inner plaintext with a non-array keymap value (nonce 0xf5x24)

cases.description: MYND-443 browser-clipper pairing-token persistence + the MYND-442 paired_at additive field (decisions.md 2026-06-21). PrefsView carries a two-record paired_extensions array (canonical key 'p', between last_backup_at and saved_views/screen_capture_protection) — record 1 has NO paired_at (the pre-feature, byte-identical encoding; revoked=true) and record 2 has paired_at set (revoked=false). Pins: (a) the per-record canonical key order extension_id < paired_at < revoked < token_value, with paired_at emitted as a bare decimal u64 (1750000000) in its slot; (b) the omitted-when-None rule — record 1 is byte-identical to a pre-MYND-442 record so an old decoder still validates the token (forward-compat §9.5.2); (c) the array sort by (extension_id, token_value) — the Chrome-style id 'abcd…' sorts before the Firefox gecko id 'clipper@myne.md'; (d) paired_extensions (p) < screen_capture_protection (s) on PrefsView. Same vault-A inputs (root_key=0x42x32, account_hash=0x33x16); prefs_nonce=0xB1x24 (next free in the family registry). Generated by `cargo test -p protocol --lib emit_paired_extensions_prefs_vectors -- --ignored` (in protocol/src/prefs.rs).

Round-trip with encrypt-paired-extensions: the blob decodes back to a PrefsView carrying both paired_extensions records under the same root_key + account_number_hash. Verifies decoders surface the MYND-442 paired_at field from its canonical slot on record 2 (Some(1750000000)) AND its absence on record 1 (None — an omitted key decodes to None, not a parse error), and preserve the (extension_id, token_value) sort order. expected_prefs_view tokens are the full 64-hex values.

Right-panel tabs. PrefsView carries right_panel_active_tab (an Option<String> pointer) + right_panel_hidden_tabs (set-canonical: sorted+deduped) + right_panel_tab_order (sequence: verbatim), pinning the canonical key order right_panel_active_tab (r-a) < right_panel_hidden_tabs (r-h) < right_panel_tab_order (r-t) < screen_capture_protection (s), all sorting between paired_extensions (p) and saved_views (sav). Same vault-A inputs as the sibling cases; prefs_nonce=0xF6x24. Generated by emit_right_panel_prefs_vectors in protocol/src/prefs.rs.

Round-trip with encrypt-right-panel-tabs: the blob decodes back to a PrefsView carrying the active-tab pointer + the hidden-tabs set + the tab-order sequence under the same root_key + account_number_hash. Verifies decoders surface the three right-panel fields from their canonical positions between paired_extensions and saved_views, canonicalize the hidden set (sorted+deduped), and preserve the order sequence verbatim.

Local-AI prefs. PrefsView carries ai_enabled (bool) + ai_excluded_folders (set-canonical: sorted+deduped folder-path strings), the two MYP1 fields the local-ai epic added (SYNC-12/14). Both keys sort ahead of screen_capture_protection: ai_enabled (a-e) < ai_excluded_folders (a-x) < screen_capture_protection (s), pinning the canonical prefix key order. Same vault-A inputs as the sibling cases; prefs_nonce=0xA1x24. Generated by emit_ai_prefs_vectors in protocol/src/prefs.rs.

Round-trip with encrypt-ai: the blob decodes back to a PrefsView carrying ai_enabled=true + ai_excluded_folders=["Private/"] under the same root_key + account_number_hash. Verifies decoders surface the two local-AI fields from their canonical positions ahead of screen_capture_protection and canonicalize the excluded-folder set (sorted+deduped).

folder-archive archived_folders field: screen_capture_protection=true plus archive_disabled=true, archived_folders (given UNSORTED with a duplicate → canonical sorted+deduped ["Alpha/","Zeta/"]), and auto_lock_seconds=300. Pins the canonical key slot of 'archived_folders' (between archive_disabled and auto_lock_seconds — ar_ < arch < au) and its set-canonical (NFC-sorted, exact-deduped, omitted-when-empty) string-array encoding, same codec as deliberate_folders / ai_excluded_folders. An unset vault stays byte-identical to encrypt-default (omit-when-empty). Same fixed vault-A inputs as the family; nonce 0xAF.

Round-trip with encrypt-archived-folders: the blob decodes back to PrefsView{ archive_disabled: true, archived_folders: ["Alpha/","Zeta/"], auto_lock_seconds: 300, screen_capture_protection: true } under the same root_key + account_number_hash. Verifies the decoder parses the archived_folders string array at its canonical slot (between archive_disabled and auto_lock_seconds).

device_names additive map (MYND-459 / SYNC-41): two device_id-hex -> friendly-name entries constructed OUT of sort order (f9e8... inserted before 1a2b...) so the encoder's lexicographic key sort is load-bearing. device_names sits at canonical key 'd' (deliberate_folders < device_names < editor_* < screen_capture_protection); the string->string map is the folder_icons/item_colors precedent class. Same root_key + account_hash as the family; distinct nonce 0xF6x24. Proves the codec for the single-home device-name registry (both clients read/write it, so no second default-name heuristic).

Round-trip with encrypt-device-names: the blob decodes back to PrefsView carrying the device_names map, keys recovered in lexicographic order (1a2b... before f9e8...). Verifies encode->decode fidelity for the additive string->string map at its canonical 'd' slot.

Per-field LWW clocks (MYND-478, Phase 2 prefs sync). PrefsView carries the additive field_clocks map (string key -> epoch-ms u64; here the 'label' field clock plus a namespaced device_names/<key> per-entry clock) beside favorites, folder_icons and label, pinning the canonical key order favorites (fa) < field_clocks (fi) < folder_icons (fo) < label (l) < screen_capture_protection (s), lexicographic clock-key order inside the map, and bare-decimal integer values (floats forbidden). Same vault-A inputs as the sibling cases; prefs_nonce=0xF7x24. Generated by emit_field_clocks_prefs_vectors in protocol/src/prefs.rs.

Round-trip with encrypt-field-clocks: the blob decodes back to a PrefsView carrying the field_clocks map (label clock + namespaced device_names/<key> clock) under the same root_key + account_number_hash. Verifies decoders surface field_clocks from its canonical position between favorites and folder_icons and parse the inner string->integer object; a decoder that does not know the field (pre-MYND-478) tolerates it per the §9.5.2 forward-compat rule and treats every clock as absent (= 0 to the sync-protocol.md §10.2 merge).

myne#415 remote-provider quartet. PrefsView carries BOTH lexicographic neighbours (ai_excluded_folders before, archive_disabled after) so the case pins the canonical POSITION of ai_provider < ai_provider_consent < ai_provider_key < ai_provider_model, not merely their presence. ai_provider_key is present in the ENCRYPTED blob and MUST NOT cross the host->UI boundary in any implementation (protocol.md 9.5.2). Generated by `cargo test -p protocol --lib emit_ai_provider_prefs_vectors -- --ignored` (in protocol/src/prefs.rs). LEGACY CONSENT VALUE, kept for its published bytes: ai_provider_consent here is the BARE wire name, which is the shape a pre-myne-md/myne#633 vault holds and which the remote-inference gate now REFUSES. The grammar an implementation must write is pinned by encrypt-ai-consent-device-scoped / decrypt-ai-consent-device-scoped beside this case.

Round-trip with encrypt-ai-provider: the blob decodes back to a PrefsView carrying the provider selection, the consent name, the key and the chosen model, each read from its canonical position between ai_excluded_folders and archive_disabled. A decoder that mis-orders the quartet fails here rather than silently returning a shifted value. The consent value it returns is the legacy bare form; see decrypt-ai-consent-device-scoped for the device-scoped grammar the gate accepts and for the predicate that separates the two.

The DEVICE-SCOPED ai_provider_consent grammar (myne-md/myne#633). The stored value is the provider's wire name followed by the literal suffix '@device' — 'openrouter@device' here — and it is that whole string, not the bare wire name, that the remote-inference gate accepts. Identical to encrypt-ai-provider in every other byte, so a port can diff the two blobs and see that the only change is the consent value, still in its canonical slot between ai_provider and ai_provider_key. The suffix is device-local by construction: consent is not a vault-wide grant that follows the blob to another machine, so a vault synced to a second device arrives with a consent that device has not given and the gate refuses it there. A port that stores the bare wire name produces a preference that reads correctly and never opens the gate. Generated by `cargo test -p protocol --lib emit_ai_consent_scope_prefs_vectors -- --ignored` (in protocol/src/prefs.rs).

Round-trip with encrypt-ai-consent-device-scoped, plus the PREDICATE the grammar exists for. expected_consent_is_device_scoped and expected_consent_is_legacy are given for both the device-scoped value and the bare wire name encrypt-ai-provider pins, against the same provider and against a different one. A port implements two questions here: does this stored value carry the suffix AND name this provider (accept), and is it the bare name of this provider (a legacy grant, refused — it is what a pre-#633 vault holds, so recognising it is how an implementation knows to ask again rather than to fail silently). A stored consent naming a DIFFERENT provider answers no to both: the gate is an equality against the provider about to receive the text, never a flag.

The four display-formatting preferences that had no cross-implementation vector: auto_tag_enabled (on-device tag suggestion, emitted only when true), date_format, time_format and timezone (myne#279 display overrides). Each is written beside BOTH of its canonical neighbours so the case pins its slot rather than merely its value: auto_lock_seconds < auto_tag_enabled < bar_items_order; daily_template < date_format < deliberate_folders; theme < time_format < timezone < transcription_enabled. vault.prefs is canonical JSON, so key order is part of the bytes: a port emitting a correct value in the wrong slot produces a blob the reference decoder rejects. All four values are display-only: none ever enters a .myn file as a formatting instruction. They do live in this blob, which is what the case encodes, and date_format/time_format are shared across devices by design. Same vault-A inputs as the sibling cases; prefs_nonce=0xD4x24. Generated by emit_datetime_quartet_prefs_vectors in protocol/src/prefs.rs.

Round-trip with encrypt-datetime-quartet: the blob decodes back to a PrefsView carrying all four display-formatting fields at their canonical positions. A decoder that does not know one of them tolerates it per the §9.5.2 forward-compat rule and falls back to that field's default (auto_tag_enabled=false, the other three = 'follow the OS locale'), which is exactly what a pre-feature client does — the point of the case is that skipping a field must not desynchronise the positional cursor and swallow the fields that follow it.

The agent chat-history seed budget (myne-md/myne#617). An optional unsigned integer encoded as a BARE DECIMAL, pinned between both of its canonical neighbours: bar_items_order (b) < chat_history_budget (ch) < cli_enabled (cl). That slot is the load-bearing half of the field's design -- it sits in the region a decoder scans forward through, so an older client steps over it, whereas a name sorting before auto_lock_seconds would have landed in the prefix-matched run where an unknown key blinds every field behind it (protocol.md 9.5.2 schema evolution). The value 3000 is deliberately not the host's clamp ceiling: that ceiling is applied in the SETTER and is host policy rather than format, so no vector pins it. Unset is OMITTED ENTIRELY rather than encoded as 0, which every other case in this family demonstrates by carrying no such key and staying byte-identical to its pre-feature self. Same vault-A inputs as the sibling cases; prefs_nonce=0xF8x24. Generated by emit_chat_history_budget_prefs_vectors in protocol/src/prefs.rs.

Round-trip with encrypt-chat-history-budget: the blob decodes back to a PrefsView carrying chat_history_budget=3000 between bar_items_order and cli_enabled under the same root_key + account_number_hash. A decoder that does not know the field (pre-myne#617) tolerates it per the 9.5.2 forward-compat rule and treats the budget as ABSENT rather than as 0 -- absent means the host applies its own default, which is a third state distinct from 'seed nothing'. That distinction is why this case exists beside the encrypt one: a port that maps a missing key to 0 decodes this blob correctly and its own default-carrying blob incorrectly.

Set-entry removal clock, live half (myne-md/myne#613, sync-protocol.md §10.2). A set-union field carries a per-entry clock under `<field>/<entry>`, where the entry key is the FOLDED folder identity (`projects/myne/`) while the set itself holds the raw display form (`Projects/Myne/`). Pins the canonical key order deliberate_folders (d) < field_clocks (fi) < screen_capture_protection (s) with a set-keyed clock present. Same vault-A inputs as the sibling cases; prefs_nonce=0xE1x24. Generated by emit_set_removal_clock_prefs_vectors in protocol/src/prefs.rs.

Set-entry removal clock, removed half (myne-md/myne#613). The SAME clock key with no corresponding set entry: `deliberate_folders` is omit-when-empty so the set key is absent entirely, and the stamp is the whole claim that the entry was deleted rather than never held. This is the shape sync-protocol.md §10.2 resolves against a peer that still holds the entry. What this ENCRYPT case pins is that the orphan key survives the encode and is present in the plaintext, byte for byte: it does not, and cannot, pin that a DECODER preserves it, because an encrypt case never hands a port a blob to read. The decode half is asserted in the reference implementation by the round-trip in `emit_set_removal_clock_prefs_vectors`'s own module tests, and a port that wants the same assurance owes itself a decode of this blob; a decoder that dropped the orphan key would silently undo every folder deletion on a multi-device vault, and nothing in this file would say so. Same vault-A inputs; prefs_nonce=0xE2x24. Generated by emit_set_removal_clock_prefs_vectors in protocol/src/prefs.rs.

Set-entry removal clock with a non-ASCII folded key (myne-md/myne#613). Two clock keys, one ASCII and one multi-byte, beside their raw set entries. Pins two things a port can get wrong with no test noticing. First, non-ASCII is emitted as RAW UTF-8 and never \u-escaped, in both the set entry and the clock key: an implementation whose JSON writer escapes by default (many do) produces a different plaintext, a different AEAD tag, and a blob the other side cannot decrypt. Second, the multi-byte key sorts in the same sequence as its ASCII sibling, which pins that a port sorts the clock map at all and does not reorder around a non-ASCII key. It deliberately does NOT claim to discriminate byte order from code-point order: UTF-8 byte order and code-point order are identical by construction, so no case can separate them, and the only ordering a vector here could discriminate is UTF-16 code-unit order, which needs an astral character against a BMP one and is not what these two keys are. Same vault-A inputs; prefs_nonce=0xE3x24. Generated by emit_set_removal_clock_prefs_vectors in protocol/src/prefs.rs.

myne#177 periodic-notes settings: a string map keyed <period>.<setting> holding the weekly equivalents of the three daily_* fields plus the two monthly ones. Pins FOUR things a port can get wrong independently. (1) The field's canonical position, and BOTH neighbours are in this blob rather than named in prose: paired_extensions (p) < periodic_notes (pe) < reminder_horizon_days (r). An earlier version of this case named those two neighbours and contained neither, so it pinned a value alone and could not have noticed a wrong slot. (2) The lexicographic key order INSIDE the map. Read that as a statement about the ENCODER rather than about this artefact: the shipped plaintext and view are both already sorted, so nothing here records an insertion order and no port can observe one. What the case actually holds is that these bytes are the sorted form, so an implementation that emits its own source order produces different bytes whenever that order differs. The generator feeds a deliberately unsorted literal, which is where the round trip is exercised, and that is a main-repo assertion a port cannot run. (3) An UNRECOGNISED period: quarterly.folder is a period no build in the reference tree knows, and it must be re-encoded verbatim, which is what makes a fourth period free without a format change. (4) NFC: weekly.folder is fed in DECOMPOSED form (o + U+0308) and these bytes carry the PRECOMPOSED U+00F6, so a port that skips the fold fails on the blob. Daily is NOT in this map by design and keeps its three top-level fields.

Round trip with encrypt-periodic-notes: the blob decodes back to the same six entries, and a decoder that dropped or reordered a key fails here rather than silently losing a period's settings. TWO round-trip properties beyond that. quarterly.folder is a period NO build knows, and it must come back verbatim, because the format's forward-compat rule for this map is re-encode-what-you-do-not-recognise, which is the OPPOSITE of decrypt-unknown-field-tolerated one case over: an unknown TOP-LEVEL field is dropped from the re-encode, an unknown period key inside this map is not. And weekly.folder went in DECOMPOSED (o + U+0308) and comes back PRECOMPOSED (U+00F6), so the round trip is exact in bytes and idempotent in values without being the identity on a decomposed input; a port that skips the NFC fold produces different blob bytes rather than a comparison it might not make.

myne-md/myne#699 left-ribbon fields (vault.prefs). ribbon_items is Some([...]) (a CONFIGURED rail; order is the payload, preserved verbatim) and ribbon_visible is false, the only value the encoder emits because true is omitted. Pins the canonical key order ribbon_items < ribbon_visible < screen_capture_protection. Generated by `cargo test -p protocol --lib emit_ribbon_fields_prefs_vectors -- --ignored`.

Round-trip with encrypt-ribbon-fields: the blob decodes back to a PrefsView carrying ribbon_items + ribbon_visible=false + screen_capture_protection=true under the same root_key + account_number_hash. Verifies decoders surface the two fields from their canonical position between reminders_enabled and right_panel_active_tab, and that an explicitly emptied rail (Some([])) is distinct from a never-configured one (absent).
